title: Work, Energy and Power
syllabus: Work done by a constant force and a variable force, kinetic energy, work-energy theorem, power; Notion of potential energy, potential energy of a spring, conservative and non-conservative forces, conservation of mechanical energy; Motion in a vertical circle, elastic and inelastic collisions in one and two dimensions

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A particle moves along the x-axis from $x = 0$ to $x = 5\text{ m}$ under the influence of a force $F = (7 - 2x + 3x^2)\text{ N}$. The work done in the process is:

[JEE Main 2022] A bullet of mass $m$ leaves a rifle barrel of length $L$ with speed $v$. Assuming the net expanding gas force on the bullet decreases linearly from $F_0$ at the breech to zero at the muzzle, the work done on the bullet inside the barrel is:
questions.solution:
The force varies linearly from $F(0) = F_0$ to $F(L) = 0$, giving $F(x) = F_0\left(1 - \frac{x}{L}\right)$:
$$W = \int_0^L F_0\left(1 - \frac{x}{L}\right)dx = F_0\left[ x - \frac{x^2}{2L} \right]_0^L = F_0\left(L - \frac{L}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{2} F_0 L$$
Alternatively, work is the area of the triangular $F-x$ graph: $\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{base} \times \text{height} = \frac{1}{2} F_0 L$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle is released from rest from the top of a smooth sphere of radius $R$. The vertical height below the apex where the particle leaves contact with the sphere is:
questions.solution:
Let the particle descend through angle $\theta$ from the vertical apex.
By conservation of mechanical energy:
$$mgR(1 - \cos\theta) = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \implies v^2 = 2gR(1 - \cos\theta)$$
Radial equation of motion:
$$mg\cos\theta - N = \frac{mv^2}{R}$$
At the point of separation, normal reaction $N = 0$:
$$mg\cos\theta = \frac{m}{R}[2gR(1 - \cos\theta)] = 2mg(1 - \cos\theta)$$
$$\cos\theta = 2 - 2\cos\theta \implies 3\cos\theta = 2 \implies \cos\theta = \frac{2}{3}$$
Vertical descent below the highest point: $h = R(1 - \cos\theta) = R\left(1 - \frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{R}{3}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An engine pumps water continuously through a hose with cross-sectional area $A$. If the speed of water exiting the nozzle is $v$ and its density is $\rho$, the rate at which kinetic energy is imparted to the water is:
questions.solution:
Mass exiting per unit time is $\frac{dm}{dt} = \rho A v$.
The kinetic energy imparted per unit time is output power:
$$P = \frac{dK}{dt} = \frac{1}{2} \left(\frac{dm}{dt}\right) v^2 = \frac{1}{2} (\rho A v) v^2 = \frac{1}{2}\rho A v^3$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A block of mass $m$ moving with speed $v$ collides elastically and head-on with an identical block initially at rest. After collision, the fraction of kinetic energy transferred to the stationary block is:
questions.solution:
In a 1D elastic collision between two identical masses ($m_1 = m_2$), the bodies exchange their velocities completely.
The incoming mass comes to rest ($v_1' = 0$) and the target mass moves with the initial speed ($v_2' = v$).
Hence, $100\%$ of the initial kinetic energy is transferred, corresponding to a fraction of 1.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] The potential energy function of a particle in a conservative force field is given by $U(x) = \frac{a}{x^2} - \frac{b}{x}$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive constants. The equilibrium position and the binding energy at that position are respectively:
questions.solution:
Force $F = -\frac{dU}{dx} = -\left( -\frac{2a}{x^3} + \frac{b}{x^2} \right) = \frac{2a}{x^3} - \frac{b}{x^2}$.
For equilibrium, $F = 0 \implies \frac{2a}{x^3} = \frac{b}{x^2} \implies x_0 = \frac{2a}{b}$.
Potential energy at this point:
$$U(x_0) = \frac{a}{(2a/b)^2} - \frac{b}{(2a/b)} = \frac{b^2}{4a} - \frac{b^2}{2a} = -\frac{b^2}{4a}$$
Binding energy is the depth of the potential well: $E_b = -U(x_0) = \frac{b^2}{4a}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A block of mass $m$ is attached to a light spring of stiffness $k$ and held so that the spring is unstretched. If the block is suddenly released, the maximum elongation of the spring is:
questions.solution:
Let maximum extension be $x_m$. At this point, the block momentarily comes to rest, so $\Delta K = 0$.
By conservation of mechanical energy:
$$\Delta U_g + \Delta U_s = 0 \implies -mg x_m + \frac{1}{2}k x_m^2 = 0$$
$$x_m\left(\frac{1}{2}k x_m - mg\right) = 0 \implies x_m = \frac{2mg}{k}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body of mass $2\text{ kg}$ is thrown vertically upwards with kinetic energy $490\text{ J}$. If $g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2$, the height at which its kinetic energy reduces to half of its initial value is:
questions.solution:
Initial mechanical energy $E = K_0 = 490\text{ J}$.
At height $h$, $K = \frac{K_0}{2} = 245\text{ J}$.
By conservation of energy, loss in kinetic energy equals gain in potential energy:
$$\Delta U = mgh = \frac{K_0}{2} = 245\text{ J}$$
$$h = \frac{245}{mg} = \frac{245}{2 \times 9.8} = \frac{245}{19.6} = 12.5\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A particle of mass $m$ executes complete vertical circular motion at the end of a light string of length $L$. The difference in tension between the lowest and highest points of the trajectory is:
questions.solution:
At the lowest point: $T_L - mg = \frac{m v_L^2}{L} \implies T_L = mg + \frac{m v_L^2}{L}$.
At the highest point: $T_H + mg = \frac{m v_H^2}{L} \implies T_H = \frac{m v_H^2}{L} - mg$.
From conservation of energy: $\frac{1}{2}m v_L^2 = \frac{1}{2}m v_H^2 + mg(2L) \implies v_L^2 - v_H^2 = 4gL$.
$$T_L - T_H = 2mg + \frac{m(v_L^2 - v_H^2)}{L} = 2mg + \frac{m(4gL)}{L} = 6mg$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A constant power $P$ is delivered to a car of mass $m$ starting from rest. The displacement of the car as a function of time $t$ is proportional to:
questions.solution:
Instantaneous power is $P = F v = m v \frac{dv}{dt}$.
$$v\,dv = \frac{P}{m} dt \implies \frac{v^2}{2} = \frac{P}{m} t \implies v = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}} t^{1/2}$$
Displacement $x = \int v\,dt = \sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}} \int t^{1/2}\,dt = \frac{2}{3}\sqrt{\frac{2P}{m}} t^{3/2} \propto t^{3/2}$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2019] A ball is dropped from a height $h$ on a horizontal floor. If the coefficient of restitution between the ball and the floor is $e$, the total distance travelled by the ball before coming to rest is:
questions.solution:
Initial downward drop covers distance $h$.
Heights after successive rebounds: $h_1 = e^2 h$, $h_2 = e^4 h, \dots, h_n = e^{2n} h$.
Total distance traversed:
$$H = h + 2h_1 + 2h_2 + \dots = h + 2h(e^2 + e^4 + \dots)$$
Summing the infinite geometric series with ratio $e^2 < 1$:
$$H = h + 2h\left(\frac{e^2}{1 - e^2}\right) = h\left(1 + \frac{2e^2}{1 - e^2}\right) = h\left(\frac{1 + e^2}{1 - e^2}\right)$$

questions.question: A force $\vec{F} = (3\hat{i} + 4\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts on a body and displaces it by $\vec{d} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j})\text{ m}$. The work done by the force is:
questions.solution:
Work done is the scalar dot product of force and displacement:
$$W = \vec{F} \cdot \vec{d} = (3)(2) + (4)(-3) = 6 - 12 = -6\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A particle of mass $m_1$ moving with velocity $v$ collides head-on elastically with another particle of mass $m_2$ at rest. The fractional loss of kinetic energy of $m_1$ is maximum when:
questions.solution:
Velocity of $m_1$ after 1D elastic collision with stationary $m_2$ is $v_1' = \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)v$.
Fractional kinetic energy retained by $m_1$ is $\left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2$.
Fractional energy lost by $m_1$ (transferred to $m_2$):
$$\Delta K / K_0 = 1 - \left(\frac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2}\right)^2 = \frac{4m_1 m_2}{(m_1 + m_2)^2}$$
This value achieves its maximum possible value of 1 when $m_1 = m_2$.

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body of mass $0.5\text{ kg}$ travels in a straight line with velocity $v = k x^{3/2}$, where $k = 5\text{ m}^{-1/2}\text{s}^{-1}$. The work done by the net force during its displacement from $x = 0$ to $x = 2\text{ m}$ is:
A force $\vec{F} = -k(y\hat{i} + x\hat{j})$ acts on a particle. The nature of this force field is:
questions.solution:
A 2D force field is conservative if $\frac{\partial F_x}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial F_y}{\partial x}$.
Here, $F_x = -ky \implies \frac{\partial F_x}{\partial y} = -k$.
$F_y = -kx \implies \frac{\partial F_y}{\partial x} = -k$.
Since the cross partial derivatives are equal, $\vec{\nabla} \times \vec{F} = 0$, indicating that the force field is conservative ($U = kxy$).

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] An electric motor produces a tension of $4500\text{ N}$ in a hoisting cable and rolls it at a rate of $2\text{ m/s}$. The output power of the motor is:
questions.solution:
Output power is the product of tension and hoisting speed:
$$P = T v = 4500\text{ N} \times 2\text{ m/s} = 9000\text{ W} = 9\text{ kW}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A pendulum bob of mass $m$ is held horizontally and released from rest. The tension in the string when it reaches the lowest point is:
questions.solution:
By conservation of mechanical energy from horizontal to lowest position:
$$mgL = \frac{1}{2}mv^2 \implies \frac{mv^2}{L} = 2mg$$
At the lowest point, tension supports gravity and provides centripetal acceleration:
$$T - mg = \frac{mv^2}{L} \implies T = mg + 2mg = 3mg$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] Two springs $A$ and $B$ have stiffness constants $k_A$ and $k_B$ with $k_A = 2 k_B$. If both springs are stretched by applying the same tensile force $F$, the ratio of elastic potential energies stored $\frac{U_A}{U_B}$ is:
questions.solution:
Stored potential energy in terms of tensile force is $U = \frac{F^2}{2k}$.
For equal applied force $F$:
$$\frac{U_A}{U_B} = \frac{k_B}{k_A} = \frac{k_B}{2k_B} = \frac{1}{2}$$

questions.question: A particle moves along a closed circular track under the action of a friction force of magnitude $f_k$. In one full revolution around the circle of radius $R$, the work done by the friction force is:
questions.solution:
Friction is a non-conservative path-dependent force that opposes the instantaneous velocity at every infinitesimal displacement $d\vec{s}$:
$$W = \oint \vec{f}_k \cdot d\vec{s} = -f_k \oint ds = -f_k (2\pi R) = -2\pi R f_k$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A body of mass $M$ splits into two fragments of masses $m$ and $(M - m)$ by an internal explosion. If the total kinetic energy generated during the explosion is $E$, the kinetic energy acquired by mass $m$ is:
questions.solution:
From conservation of linear momentum starting from rest:
$$|p_1| = |p_2| = p$$
Kinetic energies: $K_1 = \frac{p^2}{2m}$ and $K_2 = \frac{p^2}{2(M - m)}$.
Total energy: $E = K_1 + K_2 = \frac{p^2}{2}\left( \frac{1}{m} + \frac{1}{M - m} \right) = \frac{p^2}{2}\left( \frac{M}{m(M - m)} \right)$.
$$K_1 = \frac{p^2}{2m} = E \left( \frac{m(M - m)}{M} \right) \frac{1}{m} = \left( \frac{M - m}{M} \right)E$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A block of mass $m = 1\text{ kg}$ is dropped from a height $h = 0.4\text{ m}$ above the free top end of a vertical light spring of force constant $k = 400\text{ N/m}$. Find the maximum compression (in meters) produced in the spring (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
Let maximum compression be $x$.
By conservation of mechanical energy between the release point and maximum compression:
$$mg(h + x) = \frac{1}{2}k x^2$$
$$(1)(10)(0.4 + x) = \frac{1}{2}(400) x^2$$
$$4 + 10x = 200x^2 \implies 200x^2 - 10x - 4 = 0 \implies 100x^2 - 5x - 2 = 0$$
$$(20x + 5)(5x - 2) = 0 \implies x = \frac{2}{5} = 0.2\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2023] A block of mass $2\text{ kg}$ initially at rest is pulled along a smooth horizontal surface by a constant horizontal force of $6\text{ N}$. Find the instantaneous power (in Watts) delivered by the force at $t = 4\text{ s}$.
questions.solution:
Acceleration of the block:
$$a = \frac{F}{m} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\text{ m/s}^2$$
Velocity at $t = 4\text{ s}$:
$$v = at = 3 \times 4 = 12\text{ m/s}$$
Instantaneous power:
$$P = F v = 6\text{ N} \times 12\text{ m/s} = 72.0\text{ W}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2021] A ball is dropped from a height $h = 20\text{ m}$ onto a hard horizontal ground. If the coefficient of restitution is $e = 0.5$, find the maximum height (in meters) reached by the ball after its second bounce (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$).
questions.solution:
Rebound height after $n$ collisions is given by $h_n = e^{2n} h$.
For the second bounce ($n = 2$):
$$h_2 = e^4 h = (0.5)^4 \times 20 = \frac{1}{16} \times 20 = \frac{5}{4} = 1.25\text{ m}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2020] A particle moves in the $xy$-plane under a force $\vec{F} = (2x\hat{i} + 3y^2\hat{j})\text{ N}$. Find the work done (in Joules) by this force in moving the particle from the origin $(0, 0)$ to the position $(3\text{ m}, 2\text{ m})$.
questions.solution:
Work done along the path:
$$W = \int_{(0,0)}^{(3,2)} \vec{F} \cdot d\vec{r} = \int_0^3 2x\,dx + \int_0^2 3y^2\,dy$$
$$W = \left[ x^2 \right]_0^3 + \left[ y^3 \right]_0^2 = (3^2 - 0) + (2^3 - 0) = 9 + 8 = 17.0\text{ J}$$

questions.question: [JEE Main 2022] A small bob of mass $m = 0.2\text{ kg}$ is tied to an inextensible light string of length $L = 1.0\text{ m}$ to form a vertical pendulum. Find the minimum horizontal speed (in $\text{m/s}$) that must be imparted to the bob at its lowest point to loop a complete vertical circle (take $g = 10\text{ m/s}^2$, express answer to two decimal places).
questions.solution:
Minimum speed required at the bottom to complete a full vertical circle:
$$v_{\min} = \sqrt{5gL} = \sqrt{5 \times 10 \times 1.0} = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}\text{ m/s}$$
$$v_{\min} \approx 5 \times 1.4142 = 7.07\text{ m/s}$$
